Select a constructor
Your constructors (the yellow bulldozers) build everything. Left-click one to select it; its build menu opens bottom right.
Lay out an extractor

With the constructor selected, move the mouse over a deposit (woods, iron or copper ore, an oil field). The right extractor appears next to it: click to place it. You pay right away. Or press Auto-expand and let the constructor choose.
Let the constructor build it

Nothing builds itself: the constructor drives to the site and must stay there until it is done. The label above the site says what it waits for. If the constructor wandered off, select it and right-click the site.
Get goods home
Haulers drive what extractors dig up back to your command center along a supply line (drawn on the ground). Goods count only once they arrive. Losing haulers to raiders loses their cargo.
Build power
Extractors and factories slow down without power. The top bar shows supply/demand in MW. Build a power plant (it burns a little oil); pylons carry the grid out to far extractors.
Let constructors expand for you

Select a constructor and press Auto-expand (G). It keeps building extractors, power and roads on its own and spends from your bank. The panel on the left shows what each one is doing and how much to keep in reserve.
Grow the city to Industrial
Deliveries feed your city (panel on the right). A fed, powered city grows and earns science; at 150 science it reaches Industrial (tier 2), which unlocks T2 buildings, units and paved roads.
Trade with a faction
In the City panel, pick a faction, choose what to give and get, and propose. The verdict (good, fair, bad) is judged at your own prices. Trade grows your city faster than digging alone.
Build an army
Build a vehicle factory and produce tanks. Park some near far extractors and supply lines: raiders go for haulers first.

Basics and controls

You run a frontier city. You do not place houses: the city builds itself when goods reach it. Your job is the economy around it (extractors, supply lines, power), trade, and the army that protects it.

[b]Mouse:[/b] left-click selects, drag selects many, right-click orders (move, attack, build, escort). Double-click selects all units of a kind on screen. Right-drag draws a line for the selected units; Shift queues orders. Army orders (fight, patrol, guard...) are under [b]Unit orders[/b].
[b]Camera:[/b] W A S D move, the mouse wheel zooms, Q and E rotate.
[b]Groups:[/b] Ctrl+number saves a selection, the number recalls it.
[b]Building:[/b] R rotates a blueprint, right-click cancels it.
[b]Help:[/b] F1 opens this manual.
Constructors and building

Constructors build every structure. Select one to open its build menu; hover a button to see what the building does, its cost and its tier.

Placing a building pays for it at once and lays out a site. [b]The site only grows while a constructor stands next to it[/b]: the constructor that placed it drives there on its own. If you send it elsewhere, the site waits; select a constructor and right-click the site to resume. The label above every site says what it waits for.

Extractors (lumber mill, mine, oil derrick) must touch a matching deposit. With a constructor selected, hovering a deposit picks the right extractor for you.

To cancel a site, select it and press the X button bottom right: you get back the materials not yet on the road.
Auto-expand

Select one or more constructors and press [b]Auto-expand[/b] (bottom right, next to the build menu) (or press G). They then work on their own, in this order:
1. run home when enemies come close,
2. finish any site nobody is working on,
3. build a power plant when the grid is short,
4. build pylons to wire far extractors,
5. build an extractor on the best free deposit: the commodity you have the fewest extractors and the smallest stock of, close to a command center,
6. pave the longest supply route (from Industrial on).
They also order a hauler when extractors outnumber haulers two to one.

[b]It spends your bank.[/b] The panel on the left shows every auto constructor, what it is doing and what it has spent. [b]Keep in bank[/b] sets how much of each commodity it must leave you. It skips deposits more than 45 m from a command center unless your armed units guard them, and skips spots with enemies nearby.

Giving an auto constructor an order pauses it until the order is done. Turn it off with the same button or All off.
Resources

Four commodities, shown in the top-left bar (hover them):
[b]Timber[/b]: woods, lumber mill. Buildings and roads.
[b]Iron[/b]: iron ore, mine. Buildings and vehicles.
[b]Copper[/b]: copper ore, mine. Power, pylons, advanced units.
[b]Oil[/b]: oil field, oil derrick. Fuel for power plants and haulers.

Deposits run dry over time; their look shows how much is left. Part of every delivery goes to the city warehouse to feed citizens, the rest to your bank.
Supply lines and haulers

Extractors fill a small output buffer (the gauge above them shows it). [b]Trucks[/b] (haulers) drive the goods to the closest command center (the depot) along a supply line drawn on the ground; goods count only when they arrive. A full extractor [b]stops[/b] until a truck comes, so keep enough trucks, or a storage next to it.

Trucks also carry building materials out to sites. Sites inside the [b]yard[/b] (about 9 m around a command center) get materials straight away; sites further out wait for a truck, so far expansion is slower and needs more trucks.

Trucks are run automatically by the job board (see Delivery jobs). Right-click an extractor or storage with a truck selected to dedicate it to that route; right-click the command center to return it to automatic work. Raiders target trucks: lost cargo is gone, and the raider keeps part of it.
Roads

Every supply route starts as a dirt track. Select an extractor and use its Road button to upgrade its route: paved road (x1.4 hauler speed, needs Industrial) and railway (x2, needs Electric). Cost grows with the length of the route. Auto-expanding constructors pave the longest dirt routes when you can afford it.
Power

The top bar shows power supply / demand in MW. Extractors, factories and the city draw power; without enough, extraction drops to a fraction, factories slow down and the city earns less science.\n\nCommand centers make a little power. [b]Power plants[/b] make much more but burn oil. Each power building has a grid radius; structures inside it are connected, and [b]pylons[/b] extend the grid to far extractors (two grid nodes connect when their circles overlap). The blueprint warns you when a spot is off the grid.
City and tiers

The city panel (top right) shows population, what the city needs, its warehouse and civil defense. Citizens eat timber, iron, copper and oil from the warehouse; a fed, powered city grows, builds workshops (faster production for you) and earns [b]science[/b].\n\nScience unlocks tiers: [b]Frontier[/b] (start), [b]Industrial[/b] at 150, [b]Electric[/b] at 450. Buttons marked T2 or T3 unlock with them. If the city is attacked, civil defense posts and militia fight back and the panel calls for help.
Trade

In the city panel, pick a faction, choose what you give and what you get, and propose. Each faction has its own prices; the panel shows both, the fair price, and a verdict judged at your prices (good, fair or bad). A deal is bad when it leaves you with under 10 of something.\n\nAccepted goods travel by caravan, which can be raided. Trade agreements repeat a deal; an embargo stops trade with a faction. Factions also send you offers you can accept or refuse.
Combat and defense

Build a vehicle factory for tanks and other ground units, and turrets near what you need to hold. Right-click an enemy to attack it, right-click your own hauler to escort it.\n\nAI factions raid supply lines and far extractors first. Keep a few units near long routes and your far extractors; auto-expanding constructors also prefer deposits your armed units guard.
Aircraft and airports

Helicopters and gunships fly freely. Fixed-wing drones have limited airtime: they must land at an [b]airport[/b] to refuel, circle when idle, and crash when they run dry. Drones can only be built once you have an airport. A unit's tooltip shows its airtime.

Helper

The helper is an assistant you switch on in the panel at the top left (or press [b]H[/b]). It starts off. While it is on it:
1. [b]runs the economy:[/b] puts idle constructors on auto-expand and keeps three constructors, orders a freight train when far extractors call for one, and recycles trucks that had nothing to do for a minute,
2. [b]builds an army:[/b] queues the strongest combat units your bank can spare at your factories, up to the [b]Army size[/b] you set (and asks a constructor for a vehicle factory if you have none). They wait at the factory rally point,
3. [b]scouts:[/b] keeps one scout buggy visiting the parts of the map nobody has seen lately; it holds fire and turns back from enemies,
4. [b]guards constructors:[/b] it remembers every enemy your units have seen. A constructor whose path passes near them is rerouted around them; one whose destination is threatened is held back and resumes the order once the way is clear; one that enemies come close to runs to the nearest safe command center. Warnings appear in the panel and the hint bar; click one to look.

[b]It never attacks.[/b] It gives no attack orders, its scout holds fire, and its units only fight back like any idle unit at war. It never starts a war and treats factions under a pact or alliance as friends.

[b]Keep in bank[/b] sets, per commodity, what the helper (and auto-expand while the helper is on) must leave you. Your own orders always win: an order you give a constructor replaces the helper's, and turning auto-expand off on a constructor keeps the helper from turning it back on. Switching the helper off hands everything back.

Command your army

Select some units and hold the right mouse button while dragging: they spread out along the line you draw. Or press P and click to patrol, or B to patrol around your base and extractors. F1 > Unit orders lists every order.
Tip: hold right-click and drag to line these units up. F = fight your way there, P = patrol, B = patrol your base, V = guard, Z = retreat, L/K = fire stance / hold position. Shift queues orders.
Unit orders and formations

[b]Line up:[/b] with units selected, hold the right mouse button and drag. Rings show where each unit will stand; let go and they spread out evenly along the line. A short line makes several rows, on the side the units come from. A plain right-click still moves or attacks.
[b]Queue:[/b] hold Shift while giving orders to add them after the current ones. Lines on the ground under selected units show their orders: green move, red fight, blue patrol, yellow guard.

The buttons under a selection (and their keys):
[b]Fight (F):[/b] click a spot; the units go there and fight whatever they meet on the way, then carry on. Drag with the left button to fight into a line.
[b]Patrol (P):[/b] click a spot to patrol between there and here. Shift-click adds more patrol points; the units loop through them and fight what they find.
[b]Patrol base (B):[/b] the units loop around your city and out past every extractor and outlying building, spread along the loop.
[b]Guard (V):[/b] click one of your units or buildings; the guards stay with it and fight enemies that come near.
[b]Retreat (Z):[/b] back to the nearest command center without stopping to fight.
[b]Stop (X):[/b] drop all orders.
[b]Fire stance (L):[/b] fire at will, return fire (only shoot back at whoever hits them) or hold fire.
[b]Hold position (K):[/b] idle units shoot what is in range but never chase.

Control groups: Ctrl+number saves a selection, the number recalls it. Double-click a unit to select all of its kind on screen.

[b]Changing keys:[/b] put a [keys] section in controls.cfg in the game's user folder, e.g. command_patrol="O". The names are command_fight, command_patrol, command_guard, command_patrol_base, command_stop, command_retreat, command_fire_stance and command_hold_position.

Limits and match end

Matches have caps so nobody can build up forever.

[b]Unit cap.[/b] Every unit takes unit slots: constructors, haulers, scouts, raiders and drones 1, tanks and missile trucks 2, artillery and helicopters 3, heavy tanks and gunships 4, battle tanks 5. Militia and trade caravans are free. The top bar shows [b]Units used/cap[/b]. Units in a factory queue count as soon as they are ordered. At the cap, factories refuse new orders (yours, the helper's and the AI's alike) until you lose units. Your cap is 150 slots, but all players share a match cap of 400, so in a 4-player match everyone gets 100.

[b]City population cap.[/b] Each tier has a largest city size: Frontier 60, Industrial 100, Electric 130 citizens. The city panel shows [b][max N][/b]; when it is full it stops growing and building houses until the next tier.

[b]Match end.[/b] The clock in the top bar counts down 45 minutes. When the last resource deposit on the map runs dry, a 5-minute countdown starts instead if that is sooner. When time runs out the best score wins (equal scores are a draw). Score = citizens + unit slots in use + 5 per finished building + science / 10; hover the clock to see yours. Destroying every enemy still wins at once.

Modders and map makers change these numbers in data/caps.json (a map can override them) and data/tiers.json.

Delivery jobs and recycling

Your trucks share one [b]job board[/b]. Twice a second every free truck is matched to the job worth the most per second of driving: materials for a remote site come first, then goods waiting at extractors and storages. A job is worth more when the goods are valuable, when the extractor is full and standing still, when your city is short of that commodity, and when you set the building's [b]Priority[/b] to high (select it, Priority button). Routes where a truck was destroyed are avoided for a while.

A truck with no job does not sit at the depot: it [b]stands by[/b] next to the extractor that will have a load ready soonest. Only when nothing anywhere will fill up does it [b]park[/b] at the depot. The city panel counts working, standing-by and parked trucks and says how many trucks your extractors keep busy.

Every truck costs a little oil [b]upkeep[/b] per minute, working or not. When some trucks had nothing to do for a whole minute, the city panel offers to [b]recycle[/b] them: they drive to the depot and you get [b]75%[/b] of their cost back. Select trucks or a train and use Recycle to do it by hand.
Storage yards

A [b]storage[/b] (built by constructors) holds up to 120 goods of one commodity. Every extractor of that commodity within about 12 m feeds it by [b]conveyor[/b] (dashed lines on the minimap), so the extractor never stops even when no truck comes for a while. Trucks collect from a storage only in loads of 8 or more, and trains love them: one stop, a full load.

Select a storage to pick the commodity it keeps (Auto takes whatever arrives first until it is empty) and its priority. A storage is worth it for clusters of two or more extractors far from the depot. Auto-expanding constructors build one there on their own. Destroying a storage spills its goods and the attacker keeps part of them.
Freight trains

A [b]freight train[/b] (command center, needs Industrial) costs more than a truck but carries 40 goods, four truckloads, and runs twice as fast. It runs a [b]loop[/b]: depot, then up to three extractors or storages, and back.

It needs track. The first time it runs a leg it [b]lays rail[/b] as it goes, slowly, paying 3 iron and 1 timber per 10 m from your stock; it waits when you run out. Once a leg is built every train runs it at full speed.

A new train picks its own line: the busiest far extractors and storages no other train serves. Right-click your extractors or storages with the train selected to add or remove stops, and right-click a command center to move its depot; the Auto line button hands the planning back. Trucks leave the stops of a train alone unless they overflow.

When to use what: trucks are cheap and flexible for scattered extractors close to home; a storage plus a train is best for a far cluster. A train is a big target, so guard its line. Trains cost 0.5 oil/min upkeep and can be recycled like trucks.
